description: Curated priority tiers for gap ranking in the MITRE coverage assessment. Tier 1 = highest-prevalence techniques a SOC should detect first; tier 2 = very common; tier 3 = common. Techniques not listed here rank below tier 3. Enterprise-only in v1 (ICS/Mobile prioritization deferred until curated actor data exists for them). Static in v1; org-overridable later via the mitre_settings pattern.

tier_meaning.1: Top prevalence across multiple independent threat reports; near-universal in intrusions
tier_meaning.2: Very common; standard component of ransomware/intrusion playbooks

sources.name: Red Canary Threat Detection Report (2025 edition, top-technique rankings)
CISA #StopRansomware joint advisories (AA-series, observed TTP tables)
Picus Red Report (annual top-10 most prevalent techniques from malware analysis)
Verizon Data Breach Investigations Report (initial-access and action varieties)
Mandiant M-Trends (most frequently seen techniques in IR engagements)

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.why: Perennial #1-3 across detection reports; default post-exploitation tooling on Windows

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: Windows Command Shell
techniques.why: Ubiquitous execution primitive in commodity and targeted intrusions

techniques.name: Windows Management Instrumentation
techniques.why: Standard living-off-the-land execution and lateral movement channel

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.why: Most common persistence mechanism in ransomware advisories

techniques.name: Process Injection
techniques.why: Core defense-evasion/privilege technique of commodity malware families

techniques.name: OS Credential Dumping: LSASS Memory
techniques.why: Primary credential-theft step preceding lateral movement in most intrusions

techniques.name: Obfuscated Files or Information
techniques.why: Near-universal payload obfuscation; consistently top-5 in malware-derived rankings

techniques.name: Masquerading
techniques.why: Renamed/lookalike binaries appear across most incident reports

techniques.name: System Binary Proxy Execution: Rundll32
techniques.why: Most abused signed-binary proxy; long-running top-10 detection-report entry

techniques.name: Modify Registry
techniques.why: Standard persistence/configuration-tampering step; top-10 in malware-derived rankings

techniques.name: Remote Services: Remote Desktop Protocol
techniques.why: Dominant lateral-movement and initial-access vector in ransomware advisories

techniques.name: Valid Accounts
techniques.why: Stolen/valid credentials are a leading initial-access vector in DBIR and IR data

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.why: Leading initial-access vector alongside credential abuse and exploitation

techniques.name: Data Encrypted for Impact
techniques.why: The ransomware impact technique itself; final objective of the most damaging intrusions

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Tools
techniques.why: EDR/AV tampering is a standard pre-encryption step in ransomware playbooks (formerly T1562.001, restructured in ATT&CK v19)

techniques.name: Ingress Tool Transfer
techniques.why: Attacker toolkits are staged onto hosts in nearly every hands-on-keyboard intrusion

techniques.name: Application Layer Protocol: Web Protocols
techniques.why: Default C2 transport for commodity and custom implants

techniques.name: User Execution: Malicious File
techniques.why: Companion to phishing delivery; extremely common execution entry point

techniques.name: Boot or Logon Autostart Execution: Registry Run Keys / Startup Folder
techniques.why: Classic persistence staple across commodity malware

techniques.name: Create or Modify System Process: Windows Service
techniques.why: Common persistence/privilege-escalation mechanism, incl. ransomware deployment

techniques.name: Account Manipulation
techniques.why: Frequent in identity/cloud intrusions (added credentials, MFA tampering)

techniques.name: Brute Force
techniques.why: Password spraying/stuffing against exposed services remains a common access vector

techniques.name: Inhibit System Recovery
techniques.why: Shadow-copy/backup deletion is a signature pre-encryption ransomware step

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
techniques.why: Double-extortion exfiltration (Rclone/MEGA et al.) in most ransomware cases

techniques.name: External Remote Services
techniques.why: VPN/RDP-gateway access with valid credentials is a top ransomware entry point

techniques.name: Exploit Public-Facing Application
techniques.why: Top initial-access vector in recent DBIR/M-Trends (edge-device exploitation wave)

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.why: Primary lateral-movement channel for ransomware deployment (PsExec-style)

techniques.name: Remote Access Tools
techniques.why: Legitimate RMM tools (AnyDesk, ScreenConnect) heavily abused for persistence/C2

techniques.name: Unsecured Credentials: Credentials In Files
techniques.why: Credential harvesting from files/shares is routine post-access behavior

techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Link
techniques.why: Link-based phishing rivals attachments as a delivery vector

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over C2 Channel
techniques.why: Common quiet-exfiltration path when no separate exfil channel is staged

techniques.name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
techniques.why: Staging with 7-Zip/WinRAR precedes exfiltration in many IR reports

techniques.name: Disable or Modify Tools: Clear Windows Event Logs
techniques.why: Routine anti-forensics step; cheap high-signal detection (formerly T1070.001, restructured in ATT&CK v19)

techniques.name: Account Discovery: Domain Account
techniques.why: AD enumeration (net/AdFind/SharpHound) precedes privilege escalation

techniques.name: Domain Trust Discovery
techniques.why: Standard AD attack-path reconnaissance in ransomware intrusions

techniques.name: Create Account: Local Account
techniques.why: Backup-access persistence commonly noted in ransomware advisories

techniques.name: Adversary-in-the-Middle
techniques.why: LLMNR/NBT-NS poisoning and relay attacks remain effective on flat networks

techniques.name: Network Service Discovery
techniques.why: Internal scanning is a reliable early lateral-movement indicator

techniques.name: System Information Discovery
techniques.why: Near-universal malware recon step; useful low-cost detection layer

techniques.name: Encrypted Channel
techniques.why: Encrypted C2 is standard; detection relies on the network telemetry this ranks
